title: Cardinals, Rockies stage silent protest with crooked hats after umpire clash over hat angle
dek: Cardinals and Rockies players wore their hats tilted in silent protest on Saturday night following a Friday confrontation in which home-plate umpire Doug Eddings instructed rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to straighten his cap, leading to manager Oliver Marmol's ejection. The incident exposed tension over umpire authority to enforce unwritten rules on uniform details.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Umpire Doug Eddings ordered rookie Hancel Rincon to straighten his tilted cap during his MLB debut, leading to manager Oliver Marmol's ejection when he defended the pitcher.
bottom_line: Whether MLB issues a statement on umpire discretion in uniform enforcement or remains silent will clarify whether Eddings acted within his authority or overstepped. The protest signals player dissent over the decision and the power to enforce unwritten rules.
body:
On Friday night, home-plate umpire Doug Eddings instructed 24-year-old rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to wear his cap straight during his MLB debut in the sixth inning. When Rincon entered the game, his cap was tilted slightly to the left, per CBS Sports reporting. Eddings instructed the catcher to tell Rincon to straighten his hat, and the pitcher complied.
Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol came out to defend Rincon and was ejected for arguing with Eddings. According to CBS Sports, Marmol called the order a "power-hungry move." After the game, Marmol told reporters: "I had an issue with Doug. Just Doug. He took it upon himself to tell our rookie pitcher the kid's not going to wear his hat on my field that way." Marmol cited Dontrelle Willis, CC Sabathia, and Pedro Strop as examples of pitchers who have worn their caps tilted much more. The Cardinals defeated the Rockies 7-6 on Friday night.
Eddings told reporters he did not know if it was an official rule but called it "a little unwritten rule."  Eddings said pitchers cannot wear caps backwards like catchers, and if it is a distraction, it should be addressed.
Rincon said through an interpreter: "I've been pitching with my hat like that. It's not an excuse. But I had no idea why he told me to do it," per CBS Sports. Rincon surrendered three runs and recorded one out before being removed. When his replacement, Justin Bruihl, took the mound after Marmol voiced further displeasure to Eddings, Eddings gave Bruihl a pitch clock violation, which led to Marmol's ejection.
MLB Rule 3.Rules 3.03(g) and (h) cover potential distractions, specifically forbidding any pattern that imitates or suggests the shape of a baseball and glass buttons and polished metal.
On Saturday night, Cardinals players and staff wore their hats off-center in the dugout in silent protest, joined by a few members of the Rockies, per Yahoo MLB reporting.
